## Appearance

Nell is a tall, slender young woman with a delicate, fine complexion, freckles, and large, expressive gray eyes. Originally wearing her intense red hair in long braids or a short crop, it darkens as she matures into a soft, lovely auburn that curls around her face. She possesses a prominent brow, a neat nose, a sharp chin, and an expressive, graceful posture.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P13](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0013), [v1 c2 P14](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0014), [v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034), [v1 c27 P36](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0036), [v1 c31 P15](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0015), [v1 c34 P3](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0003), [v2 c1 P0](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0000), [v2 c28 P5](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0005), [v4 c33 P10](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0010)_

## Personality

Passionate, imaginative, and loquacious, Nell lives deeply in her inner world of fantasy and creative romance. Though prone to dramatic outbursts, quick temper, and occasional forgetfulness, she is fiercely loyal, generous, and earnest in her desire to do good. She possesses a deep sensitivity to beauty, an infectious enthusiasm for life, and a strong sense of duty that guides her through hardships.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P19](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0019), [v1 c2 P24](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0024), [v1 c5 P0](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0000), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c12 P46](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0046), [v1 c14 P6](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0006), [v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P23](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0023), [v4 c15 P20](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0020)_

## History

Nell is brought to Grey Shutters on St. Brendan's Island by Obed Abernethy, due to a mix-up where his sister Thirza requested an orphan boy. Though Thirza initially intends to return her, Nell's imagination and warmth win over Obed and eventually Thirza, who decide to keep her. She settles into community life in Brierley, forms a close friendship with Isolde Pembroke, and attends local school. Despite initial behavioral trials and temper outbursts, she proves bright and dedicated to her studies, competing academically with Hugh Carrow.

After passing the Entrance examinations at the top of the Island list, Nell attends Regent's Academy in Port Marlow and earns her First Class teaching license. She returns to Brierley to teach at the local school, earning the respect of her students and launching a Village Improvement Society. After the tragic death of Obed and the failure of their bank, she forfeits a college scholarship to remain at Grey Shutters and support Thirza, taking in two orphaned twin cousins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. Eventually, with Mrs. Sowerby moving in to assist Thirza, Nell attends Wexcombe College, where she wins the Thorburn Scholarship in English. Following graduation, she marries her longtime companion Hugh Carrow and moves to a small coastal house in Seven Gulls Harbor. Though her first child, Little Kit, dies in infancy, she later gives birth to a healthy son, Little James Obed, and continues building a life filled with love, writing, and community connection.

## Background by volume

- Born in Harborough, Nova Scotia to high school teachers Edmund and Bertha Harcourt, both of whom died of fever when she was an infant  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013)</sub>
- Raised by Mrs. Thomas until age eight, helping care for younger children  <sub>[v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013), [v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014)</sub>
- Lived with Mrs. Rudge for over two years, helping care for three consecutive sets of twins  <sub>[v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014), [v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015)</sub>
- Spent four months in an orphanage at Marden before being brought to St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c2 P19](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0019), [v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015)</sub>
